item.title: Google’s Gemini Omni shows off “anything-to-anything” generation
item.description: Google’s new Gemini Omni model is drawing attention for multimodal generation that can turn prompts, images, and personal media into highly realistic AI-created scenes.

item.title: Zhipu launches GLM-5.1-highspeed API
item.description: Zhipu released GLM-5.1-highspeed, claiming production output speeds up to 400 tokens per second while retaining flagship-model capabilities.

item.title: EvoVid enables self-evolving video-language models from raw video
item.description: EvoVid proposes a self-evolving framework that lets video-LLMs improve from unannotated videos through temporal Questioner-Solver self-play.

item.title: TAPE speeds up diffusion-based video generation without training
item.description: TAPE introduces training-free temporal-aware token pruning for video diffusion models.

item.title: Pivot raises $40M to build an AI operating system for procurement
item.description: Pivot raised a $40 million Series B to expand its agentic AI procurement platform.

item.title: KPMG rolls out Claude to 276,000 employees
item.description: KPMG and Anthropic announced a global alliance that will bring Claude to KPMG’s full workforce and embed it into KPMG’s Digital Gateway platform.

item.title: BMW integrates agentic AI into global business workflows
item.description: BMW Group has reportedly integrated agentic AI into operations including fleet-order processing and procurement tooling.

item.title: Hidden Door launches Atlas for AI-assisted worldbuilding
item.description: Hidden Door launched Atlas, a creator tool for building interactive AI story worlds.

item.title: California signs AI workforce-disruption executive order
item.description: Governor Gavin Newsom signed an executive order directing California to prepare workers, small businesses, and communities for AI-driven economic disruption.

item.title: Google AI Overviews stumble on “disregard” query
item.description: Google’s AI Overviews reportedly produced chatbot-like non-answers for the search term “disregard,” then stopped showing an AI Overview for that query.

item.title: AI-generated fiction renews literary-world concerns
item.description: The Verge reported that a Commonwealth Short Story Prize selection published by Granta appears to show hallmarks of LLM-generated prose.

item.title: Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview found 10,000+ high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities
item.description: Anthropic published an initial Project Glasswing update saying Claude Mythos Preview and roughly 50 partners have surfaced more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities across critical software.

item.title: Google’s AI-heavy Search rollout runs into a visible failure case
item.description: TechCrunch reported that Google Search’s new AI-forward interface produced a broken-looking result for the simple query “disregard,” burying useful links below a large empty AI response area.

item.title: New exploit benchmarks show frontier AI agents can turn vulnerabilities into working attacks
item.description: Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team published results on ExploitBench and ExploitGym, two benchmarks measuring whether AI agents can progress from vulnerability triggers to real exploit capabilities.

item.title: TechCrunch reports AI startups are stretching ARR claims
item.description: TechCrunch investigated how some AI startups and investors are using inflated or ambiguous “ARR” metrics to project faster growth than traditional revenue measures support.
item.category: Sources told TechCrunch that some investors know the numbers are being stretched but accept the narrative benefits.

item.title: xAI’s compute strategy intensifies the AI energy debate
item.description: TechCrunch reported that xAI’s natural-gas-heavy data center strategy contrasts with Elon Musk’s earlier solar-electric vision, while SpaceX’s filing frames orbital data centers and space-based solar as part of the long-term compute story.

item.title: Google’s AI glasses prototype shows Gemini-powered translation, navigation, and visual assistance
item.description: TechCrunch tested Google’s Android XR glasses prototype, finding promising Gemini-powered features but noting the display version is still not ready for shipment.

item.title: AI reconstruction of dead pilots’ voices forces NTSB docket review
item.description: TechCrunch reported that the National Transportation Safety Board temporarily restricted access to its docket system after people used AI to reconstruct cockpit audio from a spectrogram and transcript.

item.title: OpenAI ships major Codex update with Appshots and long-running goal mode
item.description: OpenAI’s May 21 Codex release adds macOS Appshots, productionized Goal mode, remote computer use, plugin sharing, and Codex CLI 0.133.0.

item.title: ChatGPT for PowerPoint enters beta
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a ChatGPT add-in for Microsoft PowerPoint that can create and edit presentations from prompts and source material.

item.title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.7-Max for long-cycle agent workflows
item.description: Alibaba launched Qwen3.7-Max, a flagship agent foundation model focused on stable, long-running enterprise workflows.

item.title: Microsoft introduces Plan agent in Visual Studio
item.description: Microsoft added a Plan agent to Visual Studio so Copilot can explore, clarify, draft, and refine implementation plans before changing code.

item.title: RoPeSLR speeds up long video generation with sparse-low-rank attention
item.description: A new arXiv paper proposes RoPeSLR, a 3D RoPE-guided sparse-low-rank attention framework for efficient diffusion-transformer video generation.

item.title: MONET releases a 104.9M-pair open text-to-image dataset
item.description: MONET introduces an Apache 2.0 dataset of about 104.9 million curated image-text pairs for reproducible text-to-image research.

item.title: RAEv2 reports 10× faster convergence for representation autoencoders
item.description: RAEv2 improves representation autoencoders for image generation, reporting state-of-the-art gFID results with much faster convergence.

item.title: Anthropic reportedly projects first profitable quarter
item.description: CNBC reported that Anthropic expects Q2 revenue to reach $10.9 billion and could post its first operating profit.

item.title: Reuters says OpenAI is preparing for a possible IPO filing
item.description: Reuters reported that OpenAI is preparing to confidentially file for a U.S. IPO, potentially targeting a valuation as high as $1 trillion.

item.title: Google AI Overviews are breaking simple dictionary-style searches
item.description: 9to5Google reported that Google AI Overviews can misread words like “disregard,” “ignore,” and “dismiss” as instructions instead of dictionary queries.

item.title: Grok struggles to show meaningful U.S. government adoption
item.description: The Verge, citing Reuters, reported that xAI’s Grok appeared in only three named examples across more than 400 U.S. government AI-use records reviewed.

item.title: Trump delays AI executive order over concerns about slowing innovation
item.description: USA Today reported that President Trump abruptly halted plans to sign an AI executive order hours before a scheduled ceremony.

item.title: Google DeepMind launches APAC “AI for the Planet” accelerator
item.description: Google DeepMind launched a three-month accelerator in Asia-Pacific for startups, research teams, and nonprofits using frontier AI on environmental risks.
